title: Immortal, but ever fainter

data.source: Whitehead, Process and Reality (1929), written here as a complete net of occasions. Computed, with 400 seeded trials on a circle and 200,000 on a line.

prediction: On flat content the seed rule is Whitehead's inheritance from all past occasions, with a discount, worked one step at a time: the same numbers. On a circle the two part. And the seed forgets: what it holds of an occasion fades fast, so "objective immortality" is carried by the record and not by the seed.
baseline: Whitehead's net of occasions, each a datum for all later ones (Process and Reality, 1929). Decoy: a seed that keeps only the last mark.
why: All five predictions held. Shared: inheritance from finished occasions (R5 is an ASSUMPTION in Phoenix). Left over on Whitehead's side: occasions that feel, and a past that never fades. Left over on CRR's side: a number for the fading. Whether the past still exists undiminished is ONTOLOGY and was not testable here.

forks.net with graded relevance or negative pr: not run; it would bring Whitehead closer to a discount

weighs: P1 and P2 are identities and would hold in any world.
result: On a line, the one-step chain and the reach to all past occasions gave the same seed (difference below 1e-9). On a circle with marks close together they differed by 4e-06 radians on average; with marks spread wide, by 0.108117 radians, and in 0.06 of trials by more than half a radian. The present seed held 0.5146 bits about the latest mark (simulated: 0.5141), 0.0105 bits about the mark five back, and next to nothing about the mark twenty back. From the last seed alone, 0.9856 of the mark five back stayed unknown. From the full list of seeds every mark came back exactly. A complete net of 30 occasions has 435 arrows; the chain has 29.

framework.name: Whitehead's process philosophy, as a net of occasions

precise_core: A scheme of categories in prose. Only fragments have been made exact, chiefly his geometry of regions.
proved_by_others: Others built the mathematics of regions and connection from his sketch. Nothing in the metaphysics is the kind of thing one proves.
differing_prediction: The metaphysics makes none. His separate 1922 theory of gravity did. Phoenix: "the metaphysics fixed none".
tested: Only the gravity theory was tested.
passed: The gravity theory is generally held to have failed (Will 1971). Phoenix: "the only part of Whitehead that could fail, did".
literature: A very large philosophical literature over nearly a century, with its own journals.
engineering: A descendant only: the calculus of regions used in spatial reasoning grew from his theory of extension.
admits_open_problems: He called the scheme speculative and open to revision. It names no particular open problems.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status.note: Scores are 0 to 3 on the stated scale. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth.
